description:
src/backend.rs:510-526 — ParseResult::new signature:

    pub fn new(
        parsed: std::collections::HashMap<jmap_types::Id, Vec<jmap_calendars_types::CalendarEvent>>,
        not_found: Vec<jmap_types::Id>,
        not_parsable: Vec<jmap_types::Id>,
    ) -> Self

The last two args are the same type. A backend author writing:

    Ok(ParseResult::new(parsed, not_parsable, not_found))   // swapped

…has no compile-time signal. Wire response sends "I found these blobs in
notFound" and "these blobs are notParsable" reversed — clients see
unparseable blobs as "not in your blob store" and missing blobs as
"present but not parseable as iCalendar". Both error classifications
are spec-defined but semantically opposite (§5.13: notFound triggers
"upload first, retry"; notParsable triggers "this blob is not iCalendar
data and never will be"). Client UI may treat them differently.

The struct is #[non_exhaustive] and has #[derive(Default)] is NOT applied
(it's not Default — parsed is required). External callers must use the
`new` constructor, which makes the swap risk fixed in the only-construction
path.

Fix options:

  (a) Builder pattern:
        ParseResult::new(parsed)
          .with_not_found(vec![...])
          .with_not_parsable(vec![...])
      Each method takes a single-purpose arg; can't swap.

  (b) Named fields via public-with-helper-constructor:
      Make the fields `pub` (already are at lines 502-507) and document
      that callers should use struct-literal syntax with #[non_exhaustive]
      bypass via Default... wait, ParseResult isn't Default. So this
      doesn't work; the #[non_exhaustive] + non-Default combination
      forces external callers through `new`. The current shape
      is locked.

  (c) Take a Vec<(Id, ParseResultStatus)> where ParseResultStatus is
      an enum { Parsed(Vec<CalendarEvent>), NotFound, NotParsable }.
      Constructor pivots internally. More verbose at call site, no
      swap risk.

  (d) Take `parsed` only as positional, then two `with_*` setter
      methods that mutate &mut self in-place. Compatible with
      #[non_exhaustive].

(d) is the minimum-disruption fix. (a) is the most fluent. P3 because
the swap is a one-time per-impl error caught by integration tests if
the test author thinks to write one — but a backend author who only
writes the `parsed` case ships the rest blind.

Compare the canonical mail-server's MdnParseResult precedent
(crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mdn.rs, referenced from backend.rs:498): same
shape today (3-positional new), suggesting the convention is consistent
across the workspace and a sweep into mail-server is needed if this is
fixed here.
title: ParseResult::new takes two same-type Vec<Id> positional args (not_found, not_parsable) — easy to swap
